newsitem.title: RWANDA: Bodies of three Spanish aid workers leave Rwanda.
newsitem.headline: Bodies of three Spanish aid workers leave Rwanda.

text.p: The bodies of three Spanish aid workers shot dead by Hutu militiamen in northwestern Rwanda left Kigali on Tuesday on the first leg of the flight home to Spain.

Sombre colleagues and friends sang a hymn for the three dead as the coffins were loaded aboard a C-130 transport plane of the International Committee of the Red Cross at the Rwandan capital's airport.
The plane flew to Kenya's capital Nairobi where the coffins would be transferred to a flight on to Europe, officials said.
In a statement earlier in the day, U.N. and other aid agencies reiterated they would not close humanitarian programmes in the Ruhengeri and Gisenyi areas of the northwest because of the killings.
But they said security in the northwest would be tightened after talks with representatives of the Rwandan government.
U.N. aid agencies decided on Monday not to suspend their operations in any part of Rwanda in the wake of the killings, saying they had to refuse to give in to "terrorist activities".
But other aid officials privately criticised the decision, saying that it could lead to more deaths of expatriates.
Hutu militiamen shot the three Spanish aid workers from the Medicos del Mundo (Doctors of the World) agency in the head on Saturday night in the northwestern town of Ruhengeri on Saturday night.
It was the worst deliberate attack on foreigners in Rwanda.
Three Rwandan soldiers were also killed in the attack and an American was shot in one of his legs which was later amputated.
Gunmen stormed a house where the aid workers were staying and demanded their passports before shooting the three Spaniards at close range. The American was shot as he dived under a table.

The killers were said by Rwandan military sources to have belonged to the Hutu Interahamwe militia which played a leading role in the 1994 slaughter of 800,000 Rwandans, mostly minority Tutsis, before being driven into Zaire by Tutsi rebels.
In a meeting with U.N. and other aid agencies in Kigali on Monday, a defence ministry official said human rights monitors should not complain if the Rwandan army went in to clear the area.
An aid official quoted the defence ministry official as saying in such a sweep human rights were bound to be violated.
"Our programme has suddenly slipped into an emergency phase for the moment," said Dominique Boutriau, head of programmes for Medecins Sans Frontieres (Doctors Without Borders) in Rwanda, on Tuesday.

Following the killings, the United Nations said aid work in Ruhengeri would be limited to the daytime and expatriate workers would not be allowed to spend a night in the city, close to Zaire's border.

Medicos del Mundo named the dead as Dr Manuel Madrazo, 42, nurse Maria Flors Sirera, 33, and Luis Valtuena, 30. The American is Nitin Madhav, 28, from the Pittsburgh area of Pennyslvania, who is being treated at a hospital in Nairobi.
U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan on Monday condemned the three killings, saying they underscored the need to find a solution to the problems of the Great Lakes region of central Africa.
